CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for reassessment of anxiety management, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, headache symptoms, and medication review.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a slight improvement in his anxiety symptoms since the last visit. He has increased his sertraline dosage to 150 mg daily as discussed, and he notes a reduction in the frequency of anxiety episodes, though he still experiences significant stress related to work deadlines. Mr. Smith describes feeling less restless than before, which he attributes to the higher dosage of sertraline, although he still struggles with concentration during particularly stressful times.
Sleep quality remains a challenge; Mr. Smith reports averaging 5-6 hours per night with continued interruptions, primarily due to anxiety. He has been adhering to the cognitive-behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) techniques but admits that the effectiveness remains limited. The melatonin dosage was maintained at 5 mg at bedtime, but he expresses a desire to explore additional options as he feels it has not significantly improved his sleep architecture.
Headaches continue to occur at a frequency of 3-4 episodes per week, with intensity rated as moderate, requiring ibuprofen 400 mg for relief approximately 2 times weekly. Mr. Smith notes that the headaches are still correlated with periods of heightened anxiety, but he has not experienced any new headache patterns or associated symptoms.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 150 mg daily 2. Melatonin 5 mg at bedtime 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 4. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief 5. Amitriptyline 5 mg nightly
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, and while he reports a slight reduction in work-related stress, he acknowledges that it remains a significant factor affecting his mental health. He has maintained his walking routine three times a week and is committed to mindfulness meditation, although he finds it challenging to practice consistently during peak stress periods. He has not resumed alcohol consumption and reports feeling more in control of his lifestyle choices.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Reports ongoing anxiety but with improved restlessness, persistent sleep disturbances, no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms noted. - Neurological: Tension-type headaches persist as described, no visual changes or focal neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath. - General: Persistent fatigue, no fever or weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 118/74 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert and oriented, in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact, no motor or sensory deficits. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative, maintains good eye contact; mood appears less anxious, with some fluctuations noted.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 150 mg daily, monitor response. Discuss the potential addition of a short-term anxiolytic, such as lorazepam, for acute anxiety management during high-stress periods if needed. 2. Insomnia: Continue melatonin at 5 mg at bedtime; reinforce CBT-I strategies. Consider referral for a sleep study to evaluate for possible sleep apnea if sleep quality does not improve. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue ibuprofen as needed; discuss the potential for preventive therapy with amitriptyline if headache frequency remains unchanged. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage continued physical activity and mindfulness practices; consider additional lifestyle modifications to enhance energy levels.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2027-05-01 to further evaluate symptoms, treatment effectiveness, and medication adjustments. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any worsening of symptoms or side effects from medications.
